Name: Mesher
Description: Mesher can save specific nodes as meshes instead of heightfields, and can also generate LODs.

Flubs.Name: Format
Flubs.Description: Specifies the file format for the exported mesh. Choose the format that best fits your workflow or target application.

Flubs.Name: OBJ
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh in the standard OBJ format, widely supported for 3D models and compatible with most 3D software.

Flubs.Name: FBX
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh in the FBX format, suitable for advanced workflows and supporting animation, hierarchy, and metadata.

Flubs.Name: DAE
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh in the Collada (DAE) format, an open standard for exchanging 3D assets between applications.

Flubs.Name: GLTF
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh in the glTF format, optimized for real-time rendering and web-based 3D applications.

Flubs.Name: GLB
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh in the binary GLB format, a compact version of glTF for efficient storage and transmission.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Sets the unit or normalization method for the exported mesh coordinates, determining how the model's size is interpreted.

Flubs.Name: Normalized
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh with coordinates normalized to a 0–1 range, useful for workflows that require unitless or relative positions.

Flubs.Name: Meter
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh with coordinates in meters, matching real-world scale for compatibility with engineering and GIS applications.

Flubs.Name: Kilometer
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh with coordinates in kilometers, suitable for large-scale terrain or geospatial datasets.

Flubs.Name: Topology
Flubs.Description: Specifies the type of mesh topology used for the exported model, affecting how the surface is constructed and rendered.

Flubs.Name: Tris
Flubs.Description: Generates the mesh using triangles for all faces, ensuring compatibility with all 3D engines and applications.

Flubs.Name: Quads
Flubs.Description: Generates the mesh using quadrilaterals where possible, preferred for modeling and sculpting workflows.

Flubs.Name: AdaptiveTris
Flubs.Description: Uses adaptive triangulation to optimize mesh density, reducing polygon count in flat areas and increasing detail where needed.

Flubs.Name: Vertices Per Side
Flubs.Description: Sets the resolution of the mesh by specifying the number of vertices along each side. Higher values increase detail but also file size.

Flubs.Name: Artifact Reduction
Flubs.Description: Applies post-processing to reduce visual artifacts in the mesh, such as smoothing or correcting problematic geometry.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: No artifact reduction is applied; the mesh is exported as generated.

Flubs.Name: Low
Flubs.Description: Applies minimal artifact reduction, preserving most original detail while correcting minor issues.

Flubs.Name: Med
Flubs.Description: Applies moderate artifact reduction, balancing detail preservation with improved mesh quality.

Flubs.Name: Create Normals
Flubs.Description: If enabled, generates normal vectors for the mesh, improving shading and rendering quality in 3D applications.

Flubs.Name: Create UVs
Flubs.Description: If enabled, generates UV coordinates for the mesh, allowing textures to be mapped accurately onto the surface.

Flubs.Name: UV Origin
Flubs.Description: Specifies the origin point for the UV coordinate system, affecting how textures are mapped onto the mesh.

Flubs.Name: TopLeft
Flubs.Description: Sets the UV origin to the top-left corner, matching conventions used in some graphics applications.

Flubs.Name: BottomLeft
Flubs.Description: Sets the UV origin to the bottom-left corner, standard in most 3D engines and texture workflows.

Flubs.Name: Create Walls
Flubs.Description: Creates vertical walls along the edges of the mesh, useful for generating closed or extruded terrain models.

Flubs.Name: Center Pivot
Flubs.Description: If enabled, centers the mesh's pivot point at the origin, making it easier to manipulate in 3D applications.

Flubs.Name: Level of Detail
Flubs.Description: Specifies the level of detail (LOD) for the exported mesh, allowing for simplified versions to be generated for performance optimization.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: Exports the mesh at full resolution with no LOD applied.

Flubs.Name: LOD1
Flubs.Description: Exports a simplified mesh with reduced detail, suitable for distant rendering or performance-sensitive applications.

Flubs.Name: LOD2
Flubs.Description: Exports a further simplified mesh with even fewer polygons.

Flubs.Name: LOD3
Flubs.Description: Exports a mesh with progressively lower detail, useful for very distant or background objects.

Flubs.Name: LOD4
Flubs.Description: Exports a highly simplified mesh, minimizing polygon count for maximum performance.

Flubs.Name: LOD5
Flubs.Description: Exports an extremely low-detail mesh, suitable for extreme distance or preview purposes.

Flubs.Name: LOD6
Flubs.Description: Exports the lowest possible detail mesh, retaining only the broadest features.

Name: Meshify
Description: Converts terrain into a faceted, mesh-like surface with controllable vertex density and detail sensitivity.

Flubs.Name: Meshify
Flubs.Description: Sets the number of vertices used to construct the mesh facets. Higher values produce finer, more detailed meshes; lower values create larger, more pronounced facets.

Flubs.Name: Vertices
Flubs.Description: Sets the number of vertices used to construct the mesh facets. Higher values produce finer, more detailed meshes; lower values create larger, more pronounced facets.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Randomization seed for mesh facet arrangement. Changing the seed produces different polygonal patterns and facet layouts.

Flubs.Name: Detail Sensitivity
Flubs.Description: Controls how closely the mesh facets follow the underlying terrain detail. Higher sensitivity preserves more terrain features; lower sensitivity results in smoother, more abstract faceting.

Name: Mixer
Description: Mixer allows layer-based manipulation of color textures and contains in-built masking.

Name: Mountain
Description: Mountain 是 Gaea 最通用的基础形体之一：以调制 Voronoi 与扭曲生成接近真实的山地形态，便于继续修饰与侵蚀。

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: 控制山脉整体尺度与范围。数值越大，山体越宽广。

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: 设置山脉最大海拔，决定峰顶相对高度。

Flubs.Name: Style
Flubs.Description: 指定山脉的地质/视觉风格，影响外形与表面特征。

Flubs.Name: Basic
Flubs.Description: 生成简洁、少侵蚀感的基础山脉。

Flubs.Name: Eroded
Flubs.Description: 施加侵蚀感，轮廓更自然。

Flubs.Name: Old
Flubs.Description: 模拟古老山地：棱角软化、形态更圆润。

Flubs.Name: Alpine
Flubs.Description: Creates sharp, rugged alpine features with steep faces and dramatic relief, typical of young mountain ranges.

Flubs.Name: Strata
Flubs.Description: Adds visible geological strata or layers to the mountain, emphasizing sedimentary or volcanic banding.

Flubs.Name: Bulk
Flubs.Description: 控制山体体量：偏瘦或厚重。

Flubs.Name: Low
Flubs.Description: 较纤细、体量感较弱的山脉。

Flubs.Name: Medium
Flubs.Description: 体量适中、通用的折中设置。

Flubs.Name: High
Flubs.Description: 厚重、体量大的山脉。

Flubs.Name: Reduce Details
Flubs.Description: 减少细碎表面细节，使山体更平滑、更抽象。

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: 随机种子，用于生成不同变体；其它参数不变时仅改变形态细节。

Flubs.Name: X
Flubs.Description: Offsets the mountain horizontally along the X axis, shifting its position within the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Y
Flubs.Description: Offsets the mountain horizontally along the Y axis, shifting its position within the terrain.

Name: MountainRange
Description: Range primitive quickly sets up an entire mountain terrain with shapes highly optimized for eroding large-scale landscapes.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall size and extent of the mountain ranges. Higher values create broader, more expansive ranges.

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: Sets the maximum elevation of the mountain range, determining how tall the peaks and ridges will be.

Flubs.Name: Style
Flubs.Description: Specifies the geological and visual style of the mountain range, affecting its shape, erosion, and surface features.

Flubs.Name: Basic
Flubs.Description: Generates a simple, unmodified mountain range with minimal erosion or geological detail.

Flubs.Name: Eroded
Flubs.Description: Applies erosion effects to the mountain range, creating realistic weathering, gullies, and worn surfaces.

Flubs.Name: Stratified
Flubs.Description: Adds visible geological strata or layers to the mountains, simulating sedimentary or volcanic banding.

Flubs.Name: Alpine
Flubs.Description: Creates sharp, rugged alpine features with steep faces and dramatic relief, typical of young mountain ranges.

Flubs.Name: Bulk
Flubs.Description: Controls the mass and volume of the mountain range, affecting how thick or substantial the mountains appear.

Flubs.Name: Low
Flubs.Description: Produces slender, less massive mountains with more delicate features.

Flubs.Name: Medium
Flubs.Description: Creates mountains with a balanced amount of mass, offering a natural appearance.

Flubs.Name: High
Flubs.Description: Generates thick, heavy mountains with substantial volume and broad bases.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Randomization seed for generating unique variations of the mountain range. Changing the seed produces different shapes and arrangements.

Name: MountainSide
Description: Generates a single mountain slope or mountainside formation.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall size and extent of the mountain slope. Larger values create broader, more expansive slopes.

Flubs.Name: Detail
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the amount of fine surface detail on the mountain. Higher values add more texture and small-scale features to the slope.

Flubs.Name: Type
Flubs.Description: Determines the primary form of the mountain feature to generate.

Flubs.Name: Slope
Flubs.Description: Creates a continuous, sloping mountainside, ideal for simulating the flanks of large mountain ranges.

Flubs.Name: Peak
Flubs.Description: Generates a prominent mountain peak, focusing elevation and detail toward a summit.

Flubs.Name: Style
Flubs.Description: Specifies the visual and geological style of the mountain slope, affecting erosion, layering, and surface character.

Flubs.Name: Basic
Flubs.Description: Produces a simple, unmodified slope or peak with minimal erosion or geological features.

Flubs.Name: Eroded
Flubs.Description: Applies erosion effects to the mountain, creating realistic weathering, gullies, and worn surfaces.

Flubs.Name: Old
Flubs.Description: Simulates an ancient mountain with softened features, rounded slopes, and significant erosion.

Flubs.Name: Alpine
Flubs.Description: Creates sharp, rugged alpine features with steep faces and dramatic relief, typical of young mountain ranges.

Flubs.Name: Strata
Flubs.Description: Adds visible geological strata or layers to the mountain, emphasizing sedimentary or volcanic banding.

Flubs.Name: Direction
Flubs.Description: Sets the orientation of the slope or peak, determining which direction the mountain face or ridge is aligned.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Defines the randomization seed for the node, ensuring reproducible or varied mountain shapes with each value.

Name: MultiFractal
Description: MultiFractal creates a multi-noise that can have a large level of variations. Often useful for texturing.

Flubs.Name: Fractal
Flubs.Description: Selects the type of fractal noise used to generate the terrain. Each type produces distinct shapes and features.

Flubs.Name: Noise Type
Flubs.Description: Selects the type of fractal noise used to generate the terrain. Each type produces distinct shapes and features.

Flubs.Name: FBM
Flubs.Description: Fractal Brownian Motion. Produces varied, natural-looking noise with a balanced mix of peaks and valleys.

Flubs.Name: Billowy
Flubs.Description: Creates softer, rounded, and bulbous shapes, ideal for rolling hills or smooth terrain.

Flubs.Name: Ridged
Flubs.Description: Generates sharp, jagged features, resulting in more dramatic and rugged terrain.

Flubs.Name: Auto Octaves
Flubs.Description: Automatically determines the optimal number of octaves for the fractal, balancing detail and performance.

Flubs.Name: Octaves
Flubs.Description: Specifies the number of noise layers (octaves) used. Higher values increase detail and complexity, but may impact performance.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall size of the fractal features. Lower values create larger features, while higher values produce finer details.

Flubs.Name: Relative Feature Scale
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the scale of features relative to the terrain size, allowing for proportional detail regardless of resolution.

Flubs.Name: Roughness
Flubs.Description: Determines the roughness of the fractal. Lower values result in smoother shapes, while higher values create more rugged, detailed surfaces.

Flubs.Name: Edge smoothing
Flubs.Description: Smooths the edges of the generated terrain, reducing harsh transitions and creating a more natural appearance.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Sets the random seed for noise generation. Changing the seed produces different terrain patterns while keeping other settings the same.

Flubs.Name: Variation
Flubs.Description: Selects the method of applying variation to the fractal.

Flubs.Name: Type
Flubs.Description: Selects the method of applying variation to the fractal.

Flubs.Name: SecondaryFractal
Flubs.Description: Uses a secondary fractal to modulate the main fractal, adding additional layers of complexity and detail.

Flubs.Name: SelfModulation
Flubs.Description: Applies self-modulation, where the fractal modulates itself to create more intricate and unique patterns.

Flubs.Name: Variation
Flubs.Description: Selects the method of applying variation to the fractal.

Flubs.Name: Smoothness
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the smoothness of the variation, with higher values producing gentler transitions and lower values creating sharper changes.

Flubs.Name: Contrast
Flubs.Description: Controls the contrast of the variation, increasing or decreasing the difference between high and low areas.

Flubs.Name: Damping
Flubs.Description: Reduces the intensity of variation or modulation, helping to prevent overly chaotic or extreme results.

Flubs.Name: Bias
Flubs.Description: Shifts the overall output of the variation, allowing you to favor higher or lower values in the resulting terrain.

Flubs.Name: Position
Flubs.Description: Rotates the fractal pattern, changing the orientation of features across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Rotation
Flubs.Description: Rotates the fractal pattern, changing the orientation of features across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Anisotropy
Flubs.Description: Applies directional scaling to the fractal, stretching or compressing features along a specific axis.

Flubs.Name: Offset X
Flubs.Description: Shifts the fractal pattern horizontally, moving features left or right across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Offset Y
Flubs.Description: Shifts the fractal pattern vertically, moving features up or down across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Warp
Flubs.Description: Selects the type of warping applied to the fractal pattern.

Flubs.Name: Perturb
Flubs.Description: Selects the type of warping applied to the fractal pattern.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: No warping is applied. The fractal pattern remains unaltered.

Flubs.Name: Simple
Flubs.Description: Applies basic, soft warping to the fractal, gently distorting features for a more natural look.

Flubs.Name: Complex
Flubs.Description: Applies advanced, turbulent warping, creating highly irregular and dynamic terrain features.

Flubs.Name: Relative Size
Flubs.Description: Controls the size of the warp effect relative to the overall terrain, allowing for proportional distortion.

Flubs.Name: Strength
Flubs.Description: Sets the intensity of the warp effect. Higher values produce more pronounced distortion.

Flubs.Name: Complexity
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the complexity of the warp, increasing the number of layers or detail in the distortion.

Flubs.Name: Roughness
Flubs.Description: Determines the roughness of the fractal. Lower values result in smoother shapes, while higher values create more rugged, detailed surfaces.

Flubs.Name: Attenuation
Flubs.Description: Reduces the strength of the warp effect over distance, allowing for localized or fading distortion.

Flubs.Name: Iterations
Flubs.Description: Specifies how many times the warp effect is applied, with higher values increasing the overall distortion.

Flubs.Name: Relative Anisotropy
Flubs.Description: Controls the directional scaling of the warp effect, stretching or compressing the distortion along a specific axis.

Name: Noise
Description: Noise applies controlled single-pixel noise onto the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Noise Type
Flubs.Description: Selects the algorithm used to generate noise. Each type produces a distinct pattern and character, suitable for different terrain or texture effects.

Flubs.Name: Random
Flubs.Description: Generates pure random noise, resulting in a highly chaotic and unstructured pattern.

Flubs.Name: Perlin
Flubs.Description: Produces smooth, gradient-based noise with natural transitions, ideal for organic terrain features.

Flubs.Name: Gaussian
Flubs.Description: Applies a Gaussian distribution to the noise, creating patterns with a bell-curve intensity and softer transitions.

Flubs.Name: Fixed
Flubs.Description: Generates a noise pattern based on large, finite shapes.

Flubs.Name: Micro
Flubs.Description: Creates very fine, high-frequency noise suitable for adding subtle surface detail or micro-variation.

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: Controls the maximum amplitude or elevation of the noise, affecting how pronounced the noise appears in the output.

Flubs.Name: Density
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the frequency or scale of the noise pattern. Higher density results in more frequent variations across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Relative Density
Flubs.Description: When enabled, density is scaled relative to the current resolution or context, maintaining consistent detail at different scales.

Flubs.Name: Blend Mode
Flubs.Description: Determines how the generated noise is combined with the input or base layer, affecting the final appearance.

Flubs.Name: Add
Flubs.Description: Adds the noise values to the input, increasing elevation or intensity where noise is present.

Flubs.Name: Multiply
Flubs.Description: Multiplies the input by the noise values, modulating the base layer and enhancing contrast.

Flubs.Name: Subtract
Flubs.Description: Subtracts the noise values from the input, reducing elevation or intensity in noisy areas.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Sets the randomization seed for the noise generation. Changing the seed produces a different noise pattern while keeping other settings the same.

Name: Normals
Description: Generates a normal map from the terrain for shading and downstream workflows.

Flubs.Name: Type
Flubs.Description: Specifies the method used to generate the normal map. Determines the level of detail and the intended use for the resulting normals.

Flubs.Name: Standard
Flubs.Description: Generates a standard normal map based on the main heightfield, suitable for general use in rendering and texturing.

Flubs.Name: Detail
Flubs.Description: Generates a high-frequency detail normal map, emphasizing fine surface features for use as a detail overlay or in advanced shading.

Flubs.Name: Width
Flubs.Description: Sets the horizontal resolution of the generated normal map in pixels. Higher values produce more detailed maps but increase memory usage.

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: Sets the vertical resolution of the generated normal map in pixels. Higher values produce more detailed maps but increase memory usage.

Flubs.Name: Detail Size
Flubs.Description: Controls the scale of fine details captured in the normal map. Smaller values emphasize finer features, while larger values smooth out detail.

Flubs.Name: Handedness
Flubs.Description: Determines the coordinate system used for the normal map, affecting how normals are interpreted in different rendering engines.

Flubs.Name: Left
Flubs.Description: Generates the normal map using a left-handed coordinate system, commonly used in some 3D applications and engines.

Flubs.Name: Right
Flubs.Description: Generates the normal map using a right-handed coordinate system, standard in many 3D applications and engines.

Flubs.Name: Up Axis
Flubs.Description: Specifies which axis is considered 'up' for the normal map, ensuring compatibility with different engine conventions.

Flubs.Name: YUp
Flubs.Description: Sets the Y axis as the vertical (up) direction, matching engines and workflows that use Y as up.

Flubs.Name: ZUp
Flubs.Description: Sets the Z axis as the vertical (up) direction, matching engines and workflows that use Z as up.

Name: Object
Description: Loads external object or mesh data for use inside the graph.

Flubs.Name: Mesh
Flubs.Description: Specifies the 3D mesh file to import. The mesh will be converted and rendered as a heightfield for use in terrain generation.

Flubs.Name: Relative Path
Flubs.Description: Defines the file path to the mesh relative to the project or asset directory. Ensures portability and correct asset referencing.

Flubs.Name: Position
Flubs.Description: Automatically positions the object so its lowest point rests on the terrain base, preventing it from floating or being embedded below the surface.

Flubs.Name: Drop to Floor
Flubs.Description: Automatically positions the object so its lowest point rests on the terrain base, preventing it from floating or being embedded below the surface.

Flubs.Name: Offset X
Flubs.Description: Shifts the object horizontally along the X axis, allowing precise placement within the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Offset Y
Flubs.Description: Shifts the object horizontally along the Y axis, allowing precise placement within the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Offset Z
Flubs.Description: Moves the object vertically along the Z axis, raising or lowering it relative to the terrain surface.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Group containing parameters for scaling the imported object.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Group containing parameters for scaling the imported object.

Flubs.Name: Rotation
Flubs.Description: Rotates the object around the X axis, tilting it forward or backward.

Flubs.Name: Pitch
Flubs.Description: Rotates the object around the X axis, tilting it forward or backward.

Flubs.Name: Yaw
Flubs.Description: Rotates the object around the Y axis, turning it left or right.

Flubs.Name: Roll
Flubs.Description: Rotates the object around the Z axis, spinning it clockwise or counterclockwise.

Flubs.Name: Quality
Flubs.Description: Enables or adjusts antialiasing for the heightfield rendering, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Flubs.Name: Antialiasing
Flubs.Description: Enables or adjusts antialiasing for the heightfield rendering, reducing jagged edges and improving visual smoothness.

Name: Occlusion
Description: Occlusion behaves similarly to Ambient Occlusion, but favors sedimentary processes vs. lighting.

Flubs.Name: Strength
Flubs.Description: Controls the intensity of the occlusion effect. Higher values produce deeper and more pronounced shadowing in crevices and low areas.

Flubs.Name: Octaves
Flubs.Description: Sets the number of detail layers used in the occlusion calculation. Increasing octaves adds finer detail and complexity to the occlusion shadows.

Name: Origami
Description: Origami creates a diagonal multifold pattern, and can produce a highly stylized terrain.

Flubs.Name: Amount
Flubs.Description: The amount of re-folding to be applied to the terrain. Low values create large folds; high values create tiny folds.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different noise patterns.

Name: Outcrops
Description: The Outcrops LookDev node creates rocky outcrops on any surface. You can control coverage, breakage, and surface details. Several Outcrops nodes can be layered for complex results.

Flubs.Name: Outcrops
Flubs.Description: Controls the number of unique outcrop shapes generated before repetition. Higher values create more visual diversity among outcrops.

Flubs.Name: Variations
Flubs.Description: Controls the number of unique outcrop shapes generated before repetition. Higher values create more visual diversity among outcrops.

Flubs.Name: Strata
Flubs.Description: Adds visible geological layering or banding to the outcrops, simulating sedimentary or stratified rock formations. High values increase the distance between Strata layers.

Flubs.Name: Density
Flubs.Description: Adjusts how many outcrops are placed across the terrain. Higher values increase the number of outcrops per area.

Flubs.Name: Shape
Flubs.Description: Determines the overall form and silhouette of each outcrop, affecting their appearance and how they blend with the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Chipped
Flubs.Description: Controls the amount of chipping or breakage on the outcrops, simulating natural weathering and erosion effects.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Sets the randomization seed for outcrop generation, ensuring reproducible or varied results with each value.

Flubs.Name: Variation Range
Flubs.Description: Specifies the base size of each outcrop, affecting their footprint and prominence on the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: Specifies the base size of each outcrop, affecting their footprint and prominence on the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: Controls the vertical scale of the outcrops, determining how tall or flat they appear.

Flubs.Name: Rotation
Flubs.Description: Applies random or specified rotation to each outcrop, increasing natural variation and preventing repetitive patterns.

Name: Pattern
Description: Generates repeatable geometric or decorative patterns for masking and stylized terrain work.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall scale of the pattern, affecting the size of the repeated elements across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Dot Size
Flubs.Description: Sets the size of individual dots or elements within the pattern. Larger values produce bigger dots or features.

Flubs.Name: Spacing
Flubs.Description: Determines the distance between pattern elements, such as lines, dots, or grid cells. Higher values increase the gap between elements.

Flubs.Name: Steps
Flubs.Description: Specifies the number of discrete steps or repetitions in the pattern, influencing the frequency and repetition of elements.

Flubs.Name: Direction
Flubs.Description: Sets the orientation or angle of the pattern, allowing you to rotate lines, engravings, or grids as needed.

Flubs.Name: Type
Flubs.Description: Selects the style of pattern to generate. Each type produces a distinct arrangement of elements.

Flubs.Name: Lines
Flubs.Description: Generates a pattern of parallel lines, useful for striations or directional effects.

Flubs.Name: Engraving
Flubs.Description: Creates a pattern resembling engraved or incised lines, adding fine detail and texture.

Flubs.Name: Grid
Flubs.Description: Produces a grid pattern with intersecting horizontal and vertical lines, forming a tiled appearance.

Flubs.Name: Dots
Flubs.Description: Generates a regular array of dots, ideal for stippling or point-based patterns.

Flubs.Name: Pixel Size
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the resolution or granularity of the pattern, controlling how fine or coarse the pattern details appear.

Name: Peaks
Description: Creates a mask that isolates the peaks and highest protruding parts of the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Falloff
Flubs.Description: Controls how quickly the mask transitions from the peaks and ridges to lower altitudes. Higher values create a sharper, more focused mask around the highest points.

Flubs.Name: Precise
Flubs.Description: Enables a more accurate detection of peaks and ridges, resulting in a mask that closely follows the true tips of the terrain.

Name: Perlin
Description: Perlin 是最基础的噪声。Gaea 提供面向地形设计的“地理变体”，从一开始就更适合做地貌。

Flubs.Name: Noise
Flubs.Description: 指定 Perlin 噪声风格，影响整体外观。

Flubs.Name: Type
Flubs.Description: 指定 Perlin 噪声风格，影响整体外观。

Flubs.Name: FBM
Flubs.Description: Fractal Brownian Motion. Produces classic Perlin noise with layered octaves for natural, smooth terrain.

Flubs.Name: Ridged
Flubs.Description: Generates ridged noise, emphasizing sharp crests and valleys for more dramatic, mountainous features.

Flubs.Name: Billowy
Flubs.Description: Creates billowy, cloud-like noise with soft, rounded shapes and less pronounced valleys.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: 噪声尺度。越大形状越粗、细节越少；越小细节越密。

Flubs.Name: Octaves
Flubs.Description: 噪声倍频数。越高通过叠加更多层细节而更复杂。

Flubs.Name: Gain
Flubs.Description: 控制倍频之间的振幅衰减，影响细节持续强度。

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: 设置噪声最大高度/强度，垂直缩放输出。

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: 随机种子。

Flubs.Name: Warp
Flubs.Description: Specifies the style of Perlin noise to generate, affecting the overall appearance and structure of the noise pattern.

Flubs.Name: Type
Flubs.Description: 指定 Perlin 噪声风格，影响整体外观。

Flubs.Name: Frequency
Flubs.Description: Controls the frequency of the warp, determining how often the pattern is distorted across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Amplitude
Flubs.Description: Sets the strength of the warp effect, controlling how far the noise is displaced.

Flubs.Name: Octaves
Flubs.Description: 噪声倍频数。越高通过叠加更多层细节而更复杂。

Flubs.Name: Transform
Flubs.Description: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the noise horizontally.

Flubs.Name: Scale X
Flubs.Description: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the noise horizontally.

Flubs.Name: Scale Y
Flubs.Description: The non-uniform scale of the Y axis, stretching or compressing the noise vertically.

Flubs.Name: X
Flubs.Description: Offsets the Perlin noise along the X axis, shifting its position horizontally.

Flubs.Name: Y
Flubs.Description: Offsets the Perlin noise along the Y axis, shifting its position vertically.

Name: Pixelate
Description: Converts the input into a blocky, pixelated version.

Name: Plates
Description: Plates primitive is based on a Perlin core with flat plate-like formations created in between larger Perlin-esque shapes.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: The scale of the overall field of shapes. Controls the size of the tectonic plates or regions generated by the node.

Flubs.Name: Range
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the variation in elevation or intensity between different plates, affecting the contrast and diversity of the generated regions.

Flubs.Name: Falloff
Flubs.Description: Controls the smoothness of the transitions between plates. Higher values create softer, more gradual boundaries; lower values produce sharper edges.

Flubs.Name: Warp
Flubs.Description: Applies distortion to the plate boundaries, introducing irregularity and natural variation to the shapes.

Flubs.Name: Angle
Flubs.Description: Sets the orientation or rotation of the plate pattern, allowing you to control the directional flow of the generated regions.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different plate arrangements while keeping other settings the same.

Name: Pockmarks
Description: Creates scattered pits, dents, and small impact-like depressions on the surface.

Flubs.Name: Pockmarks
Flubs.Description: Controls the average diameter of each pockmark. Larger values produce bigger pits, while smaller values create finer surface detail.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: Controls the average diameter of each pockmark. Larger values produce bigger pits, while smaller values create finer surface detail.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Sets the overall scale of the pockmark pattern, affecting how widely pockmarks are distributed across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Depth
Flubs.Description: Specifies how deep each pockmark is carved into the surface. Higher values create more pronounced depressions.

Flubs.Name: Density
Flubs.Description: Adjusts how many pockmarks are scattered across the terrain. Higher values increase the number of pits per area.

Flubs.Name: Multiplier
Flubs.Description: Scales the intensity or strength of the pockmark effect, amplifying the impact of each depression.

Flubs.Name: Invert
Flubs.Description: Inverts the effect, turning pockmarks into raised bumps instead of depressions.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Randomization seed for pockmark placement and variation. Changing the seed produces different pockmark patterns.

Name: PointCloud
Description: Exports the terrain as a point cloud in formats such as PLY, XYZ, or CSV.

Flubs.Name: Format
Flubs.Description: Specifies the file format used for exporting the point cloud. Choose the format that best fits your workflow or target application.

Flubs.Name: PLY
Flubs.Description: Exports the point cloud in the standard ASCII PLY (Polygon File Format) format, widely supported for 3D data exchange.

Flubs.Name: PLY_BINARY
Flubs.Description: Exports the point cloud in binary PLY format, offering smaller file sizes and faster read/write performance compared to ASCII.

Flubs.Name: XYZ
Flubs.Description: Exports the point cloud as a simple XYZ text file, with each line representing a point's X, Y, and Z coordinates.

Flubs.Name: CSV
Flubs.Description: Exports the point cloud as a CSV (Comma-Separated Values) file, suitable for use in spreadsheets or data analysis tools.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Sets the unit or normalization method for the exported point cloud coordinates. Determines how the point positions are scaled in the output file.

Flubs.Name: Normalized
Flubs.Description: Exports coordinates normalized to a 0–1 range, useful for workflows that require unitless or relative positions.

Flubs.Name: Meter
Flubs.Description: Exports coordinates in meters, matching real-world scale for compatibility with GIS and engineering applications.

Flubs.Name: Kilometer
Flubs.Description: Exports coordinates in kilometers, suitable for large-scale terrain or geospatial datasets.

Flubs.Name: Center Pivot
Flubs.Description: If enabled, centers the point cloud around the origin by offsetting all points so that the dataset's centroid is at (0,0,0). Useful for easier manipulation in 3D applications.

Flubs.Name: Ignore Zero Values
Flubs.Description: When enabled, points with zero or null values are excluded from the export. This helps remove empty data such as the normal low floor of the terrain from the output file.

Name: RadialGradient
Description: Generates a circular gradient radiating outward from a center point.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall size of the radial gradient. Increasing the scale expands the gradient outward, affecting a larger area of the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: Sets the maximum height or intensity at the center of the radial gradient. Higher values create a more pronounced peak in the center.

Flubs.Name: X
Flubs.Description: Specifies the horizontal position of the gradient's center. Adjust this value to move the gradient left or right across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Y
Flubs.Description: Specifies the vertical position of the gradient's center. Adjust this value to move the gradient up or down across the terrain.

Name: Recurve
Description: Recurve is a curvature-based expander that inflates and/or deflates the terrain to create stronger slopes and larger, softer formations from a given noise or terrain.

Flubs.Name: Power
Flubs.Description: The strength of the inflate/deflate operation. Higher values cause drastic shifts in shape formation.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: The amount of details to preserve. Higher values cause more prominent shapes to form.

Flubs.Name: Outward

Name: Repeat
Description: Repeat takes a shape and repeats it in a tiled pattern. It is often combined with the Seamless node.

Flubs.Name: Tiles
Flubs.Description: The number of repetitions on either axis. Controls how many times the input is tiled horizontally and vertically across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Compensate Height
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the height of each tile to prevent elevation buildup at tile seams, ensuring a smoother and more seamless repeat pattern.

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: Sets the maximum elevation for the repeated tiles, allowing you to control the overall height of the tiled output.

Name: Reseed
Description: Re-randomizes an upstream procedural node by overriding or refreshing its seed behavior.

Name: RGBMerge
Description: Combines three heightfields into a single RGB color output by packing them into separate channels.

Flubs.Name: Enhance R
Flubs.Description: Selects the enhancement method for the Red channel before merging. Adjusts the contrast and distribution of red values to improve the final output.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: No enhancement is applied to the Red channel. The input values are used as-is.

Flubs.Name: Autolevel
Flubs.Description: Automatically stretches the Red channel's values to use the full available range, increasing contrast.

Flubs.Name: Equalize
Flubs.Description: Redistributes the Red channel's values to achieve a more uniform histogram, enhancing detail and balance.

Flubs.Name: Enhance G
Flubs.Description: Selects the enhancement method for the Green channel before merging. Adjusts the contrast and distribution of green values to improve the final output.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: No enhancement is applied to the Green channel. The input values are used as-is.

Flubs.Name: Autolevel
Flubs.Description: Automatically stretches the Green channel's values to use the full available range, increasing contrast.

Flubs.Name: Equalize
Flubs.Description: Redistributes the Green channel's values to achieve a more uniform histogram, enhancing detail and balance.

Flubs.Name: Enhance B
Flubs.Description: Selects the enhancement method for the Blue channel before merging. Adjusts the contrast and distribution of blue values to improve the final output.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: No enhancement is applied to the Blue channel. The input values are used as-is.

Flubs.Name: Autolevel
Flubs.Description: Automatically stretches the Blue channel's values to use the full available range, increasing contrast.

Flubs.Name: Equalize
Flubs.Description: Redistributes the Blue channel's values to achieve a more uniform histogram, enhancing detail and balance.

Name: RGBSplit
Description: RGBSplit takes a color node and splits the Red/Green/Blue channels into heightfields. The counterpart to RGBMix.

Flubs.Name: Autolevel Channels
Flubs.Description: Automatically adjusts the levels of each RGB channel independently, ensuring optimal contrast and brightness for each channel after splitting.

Flubs.Name: Method
Flubs.Description: Specifies the algorithm used to split the RGB image into separate channels or grayscale outputs.

Flubs.Name: Average
Flubs.Description: Splits the image by averaging the values of the RGB channels, producing a single grayscale output based on the mean intensity.

Flubs.Name: BT601
Flubs.Description: Uses the BT.601 standard for converting RGB to luminance, applying weighted coefficients for each channel to match broadcast video standards.

Flubs.Name: BT709
Flubs.Description: Uses the BT.709 standard for RGB to luminance conversion, applying weights optimized for HD video and modern displays.

Flubs.Name: RedChannel
Flubs.Description: Extracts only the red channel from the RGB image, outputting its values as a grayscale map.

Name: Ridge
Description: Ridge 生成带多处断裂与剪切感的崎岖山脊线。

Flubs.Name: Scale

Name: Rivers
Description: Rivers creates a realistic network of rivers with controllable headwaters.

Flubs.Name: Water
Flubs.Description: The amount of water in headwaters. Higher values can create larger rivers.

Flubs.Name: Width
Flubs.Description: The width of the rivers. High values create wide rivers, with somewhat wide tributaries. Low values create thin rivers with thin tributaries.

Flubs.Name: Depth
Flubs.Description: The depth of the rivers. This value is independent of Downcutting.

Flubs.Name: Downcutting
Flubs.Description: Like with the Erosion node, Downcutting decides how deeply the river should cut into rock and soil while moving forward.

Name: RockMap
Description: RockMap creates a rock-like coverage mask that can be used to texture terrains on its own or combined with other Data Maps.

Flubs.Name: Coverage
Flubs.Description: The amount of rock-like formations on the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Density
Flubs.Description: The density of the rock-like formations.

Name: RockNoise
Description: RockNoise is a useful tool for generating fields of rocks with size variations and controllable density.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: The relative size of the rocks generated by the noise.

Flubs.Name: Octaves
Flubs.Description: Each octave adds smaller/subdivided rocks in between the larger ones from the previous octave.

Name: Rockscape
Description: Creates broad rocky surface formations and broken stone-like terrain detail.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall scale of the rock formations. Higher values produce larger, more expansive rock features.

Flubs.Name: Erosion
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the amount of erosion applied to the rockscape, simulating natural weathering and smoothing of rock surfaces.

Flubs.Name: Breakage
Flubs.Description: Determines the degree of fracturing and splitting in the rocks, creating more jagged and broken surfaces as the value increases.

Flubs.Name: Roughness
Flubs.Description: Sets the surface roughness of the rocks, adding fine detail and texture to the formations.

Flubs.Name: Jitter
Flubs.Description: Introduces randomness to the placement and shape of rock features, making the rockscape appear more natural and less uniform.

Flubs.Name: Clusters
Flubs.Description: Controls the clustering behavior of rock formations, affecting how rocks group together or remain isolated.

Flubs.Name: Off
Flubs.Description: Disables clustering, resulting in evenly distributed rock features.

Flubs.Name: Large
Flubs.Description: Creates large clusters of rocks, forming prominent groupings and massifs.

Flubs.Name: Small
Flubs.Description: Generates small, tight clusters of rocks, producing scattered groupings across the surface.

Flubs.Name: Shattered
Flubs.Description: Simulates shattered rock formations, with highly fragmented and irregular clusters.

Flubs.Name: Relief
Flubs.Description: Specifies the style of surface relief, affecting the sharpness and layering of the rockscape.

Flubs.Name: Off
Flubs.Description: No additional relief is applied; the surface remains as generated by the base parameters.

Flubs.Name: Sharp
Flubs.Description: Applies sharp, pronounced relief, emphasizing angular features and steep transitions.

Flubs.Name: Soft
Flubs.Description: Applies soft, gentle relief, smoothing out transitions and creating a more weathered appearance.

Flubs.Name: Stratified
Flubs.Description: Adds visible stratification or layering to the rockscape, simulating sedimentary or banded rock formations.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Randomization seed for generating unique variations of the rockscape. Changing the seed produces different rock patterns.

Description: 生成层状砂岩式阶地与沉积岩结构。

Name: Terraces
Description: Creates stepped terrace formations from the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Terraces
Flubs.Description: Controls the number and spacing of terrace steps applied to the terrain. Increasing this value creates more distinct, layered steps.

Flubs.Name: Uniformity
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the consistency of terrace step heights. Higher uniformity produces evenly spaced terraces, while lower values introduce variation.

Flubs.Name: Steepness
Flubs.Description: Sets the vertical sharpness of each terrace step. Higher steepness results in more abrupt transitions between steps.

Flubs.Name: Intensity
Flubs.Description: Determines the overall strength of the terrace effect. Higher intensity makes the terraces more pronounced in the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Seed

Flubs.Name: LOD Info

Flubs.Name: Structure

Flubs.Name: Slope

Flubs.Name: Flows

Flubs.Name: Soil

Flubs.Name: Patches

Flubs.Name: Chaos

Flubs.Name: Peaks

Flubs.Name: Processing

Description: 模拟热力侵蚀，生成岩屑坡（talus）与碎屑堆积。

Flubs.Description: Sets the maximum slope angle before material begins to move downward, forming talus. Lower angles create gentler slopes, while higher angles allow steeper terrain before shifting occurs.

Flubs.Name: Settling
Flubs.Description: Controls how quickly and thoroughly loose material settles after being eroded. Higher values result in faster, more complete settling, while lower values allow for gradual accumulation.

Flubs.Name: Sediment Removal
Flubs.Description: Determines the amount of sediment removed during talus formation. Higher values produce cleaner, sharper features, while lower values allow more sediment to accumulate, creating smoother transitions.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Sets the scale of the largest thermal erosion features in the terrain. Larger values create broader, more pronounced features; smaller values result in finer details.

Flubs.Name: Feature Scale

Flubs.Name: Real Scale

Flubs.Name: Terrain Scale
Flubs.Description: Specifies the overall scale of the terrain when Real Scale is turned off, allowing for manual adjustment of terrain size.

Flubs.Name: Verticality

Name: Thermal2

Flubs.Name: Erosion
Flubs.Description: Controls the duration of the thermal erosion process. Higher values extend the erosion period, resulting in more significant changes to the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Duration
Flubs.Description: Controls the duration of the thermal erosion process. Higher values extend the erosion period, resulting in more significant changes to the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Strength
Flubs.Description: Determines the intensity of thermal erosion. Increasing this value produces more pronounced smoothing and displacement of materials, especially on steeper slopes.

Flubs.Name: Anisotropy
Flubs.Description: Governs the directional bias of erosion and rock deposits. Low values preserve the original terrain with minimal smoothing, while high values intensify erosion, especially on sharp peaks, leading to stronger talus formation and more heavily eroded terrain. Useful for simulating environments with directional erosion influences such as wind or gravity.

Flubs.Name: Talus

Name: ThermalShaper

Flubs.Name: Influence
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall strength of the thermal shaping effect applied to the input terrain. Higher values increase the impact, blending more of the thermal shaping with the original terrain. Mid-range values provide a balance between the effect and the source terrain.

Flubs.Name: Shape
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the shaping style of the terrain. Negative values condense the terrain into sharp, concise ridges, while positive values bulk up the terrain, creating softer, more rounded features.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Sets the scale at which the thermal shaping is applied. Lower values focus the effect on smaller details and individual ridges, while higher values apply the shaping to larger terrain features, affecting broader mountain ranges.

Flubs.Name: Microdetail Preservation
Flubs.Description: Preserves fine details from the original terrain during thermal shaping. Higher values maintain more microdetail, such as rocky textures and small features, while lower values result in smoother, more uniform terrain.

Name: Threshold

Flubs.Name: Level

Name: Trees
Description: The Arboreal Node gives you the power of creating superficial forests and vegetation. These forests are part of the heightfield while being "detached" enough for various export scenarios.

Flubs.Name: Trees
Flubs.Description: Determines the output type for tree placement. 'Instances' provides individual tree positions for rendering and export. 'AreaMask' is an experimental feature that outputs a mask of tree coverage, useful for blending or exclusion but may be less reliable.

Flubs.Name: Output
Flubs.Description: Determines the output type for tree placement. 'Instances' provides individual tree positions for rendering and export. 'AreaMask' is an experimental feature that outputs a mask of tree coverage, useful for blending or exclusion but may be less reliable.

Flubs.Name: Instances
Flubs.Description: Outputs individual tree instance data for use in rendering, simulation, or export. Recommended for stable and reliable results.

Flubs.Name: AreaMask
Flubs.Description: Outputs a mask indicating areas where trees are placed. Useful for visualization and blending, but currently experimental and may produce less predictable results.

Flubs.Name: Count in Thousands
Flubs.Description: Sets the number of trees to be placed, specified in thousands. Higher values increase density and mask quality but may impact performance and memory usage.

Flubs.Name: Is Relative
Flubs.Description: If enabled, tree count scales with terrain resolution for consistent density. Recommended for predictable results at higher resolutions, but may increase resource usage.

Flubs.Name: LOD Info
Flubs.Description: Provides Level of Detail (LOD) information for tree instances, enabling optimized rendering and export at different distances or resolutions.

Flubs.Name: Tree Size
Flubs.Description: Controls the height of each tree instance. Affects the appearance of exported trees but not the mask. Useful for adjusting the final look of tree outputs.

Flubs.Name: Trim Under
Flubs.Description: Removes tree instances below a certain size threshold, clamping down on smaller or weaker trees to refine the mask and output.

Flubs.Name: Shape
Flubs.Description: Specifies the distribution pattern or type of tree shapes. 'Point' is a single pixel, 'Big' is a larger square, and 'BigOnly' restricts placement to large clusters. 'Big' is preferred for mask export, while 'Point' is better for visualization.

Flubs.Name: Point
Flubs.Description: Places trees as single small pixels, resulting in sparse and detailed distribution. Best for internal visualization.

Flubs.Name: Big
Flubs.Description: Places larger tree shapes, creating denser and more legible masks. Preferred for exporting tree masks.

Flubs.Name: BigOnly
Flubs.Description: Restricts placement to only large tree clusters, excluding smaller or individual trees for a bold mask.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Sets the randomization seed for procedural tree placement. Changing the seed produces different tree layouts and simulation results.

Flubs.Name: Growth
Flubs.Description: Controls whether trees grow near water flows ('Seek') or away from them ('Avoid'). Useful for simulating species preferences and biomes.

Flubs.Name: Seek Water
Flubs.Description: Controls whether trees grow near water flows ('Seek') or away from them ('Avoid'). Useful for simulating species preferences and biomes.

Flubs.Name: Seek
Flubs.Description: Trees preferentially grow near water sources and flow areas, simulating water-loving species.

Flubs.Name: Avoid
Flubs.Description: Trees avoid water sources and flow areas, simulating species that prefer drier conditions.

Flubs.Name: Avoid Trees
Flubs.Description: Masks out areas occupied by other tree nodes, useful for stacking multiple tree species or biomes without overlap.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: No avoidance; trees can be placed close together or overlap with other tree nodes.

Flubs.Name: Previous
Flubs.Description: New trees avoid areas occupied by the previously placed tree node, reducing overlap in stacked nodes.

Flubs.Name: All
Flubs.Description: New trees avoid all other tree nodes in the stack, maximizing spacing and separation.

Flubs.Name: Health
Flubs.Description: Controls the duration and vigor of the tree simulation. Higher health increases density and allows trees to grow into smaller valleys and more challenging terrain. Lower health restricts growth to main flow areas.

Flubs.Name: Patches
Flubs.Description: Clumps trees together into larger groups, creating stylized patches instead of individual trees. Useful for natural-looking forests.

Flubs.Name: Spread
Flubs.Description: Blurs and expands the area where trees can grow, merging small flows into larger masses and creating more natural, contiguous forest areas.

Flubs.Name: Random
Flubs.Description: Adds random noise to tree placement, scattering trees across the terrain without regard to inhibition or aspect controls. Rarely used for realistic masks.

Flubs.Name: Aspect Inhibition
Flubs.Description: Restricts tree growth on steep terrain. Not recommended when using a custom inhibition mask, as the mask provides more accurate control.

Flubs.Name: Slope
Flubs.Description: Restricts tree growth on steep terrain. Not recommended when using a custom inhibition mask, as the mask provides more accurate control.

Flubs.Name: Slope Falloff
Flubs.Description: Controls how quickly tree density decreases as slope increases. Use with slope inhibition for gradual or sharp transitions.

Flubs.Name: Altitude
Flubs.Description: Sets altitude limits for tree placement, simulating elevation-based growth restrictions. Works well with both aspect inhibition and custom masks.

Flubs.Name: Altitude Falloff
Flubs.Description: Controls the rate at which tree density decreases with altitude, enabling smooth or sharp transitions in elevation-based inhibition.

Flubs.Name: Peaks
Flubs.Description: Removes tree growth from exposed mountain peaks, preventing trees from growing in the most exposed areas.

Flubs.Name: Strict
Flubs.Description: Enforces strict adherence to inhibition rules, resulting in sharper falloff and less natural tree distribution. Use for precise, non-organic masks.

Flubs.Name: Snow Inhibition
Flubs.Description: Represents areas where tree growth is suppressed due to snow mass or adverse conditions. Controls the amount of snow mass moving down the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Dead Flow
Flubs.Description: Represents areas where tree growth is suppressed due to snow mass or adverse conditions. Controls the amount of snow mass moving down the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Consolidate Flows
Flubs.Description: Groups snow flows into larger masses, affecting how far snow moves down the terrain and influencing tree inhibition.

Flubs.Name: Bias
Flubs.Description: Directs snow flows to move less or more, affecting the inhibition of tree growth in snowy areas.

Flubs.Name: Snowline
Flubs.Description: Defines the altitude at which snow flows start, restricting tree growth above this line.

Flubs.Name: Artistic Control
Flubs.Description: Warps tree positions for a more natural, randomized look, breaking up straight flows and adding organic variation.

Flubs.Name: Chaos
Flubs.Description: Warps tree positions for a more natural, randomized look, breaking up straight flows and adding organic variation.

Flubs.Name: Blur Edges
Flubs.Description: Softens and tapers the edges of tree patches, blending them into the terrain for a more natural transition.

Description: Creates tectonic-style uplift by raising and shaping large terrain masses.

Name: Var
Description: Reads or modifies named graph variables for procedural control and automation.

Flubs.Name: Edit Mode
Flubs.Description: Specifies how the variable is used in the node. 'Consume' reads the value of an existing variable, while 'Modify' changes the value or applies an expression to the variable.

Flubs.Name: Consume
Flubs.Description: Reads and uses the value of the specified variable without altering it.

Flubs.Name: Modify
Flubs.Description: Applies an expression or new value to the variable, updating its value for subsequent nodes.

Flubs.Name: Variable Name
Flubs.Description: The name of the variable to consume or modify. This should match the variable defined elsewhere in the graph or macro.

Flubs.Name: Expression
Flubs.Description: An optional mathematical or logical expression to apply when modifying the variable. Used only in 'Modify' mode.

Flubs.Name: Default Value
Flubs.Description: The value to use if the specified variable is not set or available. Ensures the node has a fallback value.

Name: VariableBlur
Description: Blurs the input by varying the blur amount across the surface using local data or a guide.

Flubs.Name: Blur
Flubs.Description: Controls the blur radius for each pixel. The radius can vary across the image, enabling localized or mask-driven blur effects.

Flubs.Name: Radius
Flubs.Description: Controls the blur radius for each pixel. The radius can vary across the image, enabling localized or mask-driven blur effects.

Name: Volcano
Description: Generates a volcanic landform with a central cone and crater structure.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall size of the volcano feature in the terrain. Increasing the scale makes the volcano larger relative to the surrounding landscape.

Flubs.Name: Height
Flubs.Description: Sets the maximum elevation of the volcano. Higher values produce taller volcanic structures.

Flubs.Name: Mouth
Flubs.Description: Defines the diameter of the volcano's crater opening. Adjusting this parameter changes how wide or narrow the mouth appears.

Flubs.Name: Bulk
Flubs.Description: Determines the mass and thickness of the volcano's body. Higher bulk values result in a more massive and robust volcano shape.

Flubs.Name: Surface
Flubs.Description: Specifies the surface characteristics of the volcano, allowing selection between different terrain styles for the outer slopes.

Flubs.Name: Smooth
Flubs.Description: Applies a smooth surface to the volcano, minimizing roughness and erosion effects for a clean, uniform appearance.

Flubs.Name: Eroded
Flubs.Description: Applies erosion effects to the volcano's surface, simulating weathered and worn terrain with more natural detail.

Flubs.Name: X
Flubs.Description: Sets the horizontal position of the volcano on the terrain grid. Adjust to move the volcano left or right.

Flubs.Name: Y
Flubs.Description: Sets the vertical position of the volcano on the terrain grid. Adjust to move the volcano up or down.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Defines the randomization seed for procedural generation. Changing the seed produces different volcano shapes and features.

Name: Voronoi
Description: Voronoi is a staple of procedural design and creates sharp, geometric patterns. In Gaea, we've made a "geo-variant" by modifying the base Voronoi shape to fit the needs of terrain design from the beginning.

Flubs.Name: Noise
Flubs.Description: The perceptual scale of the Voronoi shapes. Higher values create more, smaller shapes; lower values produce fewer, larger cells.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: The perceptual scale of the Voronoi shapes. Higher values create more, smaller shapes; lower values produce fewer, larger cells.

Flubs.Name: Jitter
Flubs.Description: Controls the offset of the Voronoi points, ranging from perfectly symmetrical (low jitter) to highly chaotic (high jitter) cell placement.

Flubs.Name: Function
Flubs.Description: Specifies the distance function used to calculate Voronoi cells, affecting the shape and boundaries of each cell.

Flubs.Name: Euclidean
Flubs.Description: Uses the standard Euclidean distance, resulting in natural, rounded cell shapes.

Flubs.Name: Manhattan
Flubs.Description: Uses the Manhattan (grid-based) distance, producing square or diamond-shaped cells.

Flubs.Name: Form
Flubs.Description: Determines how the height or value of each Voronoi cell is calculated, affecting the resulting terrain or pattern.

Flubs.Name: C
Flubs.Description: Voronoi cells with height determined by the cell itself, creating classic cell-based patterns.

Flubs.Name: N
Flubs.Description: Voronoi cells with height determined by the nearest neighbor, resulting in smoother transitions between cells.

Flubs.Name: R
Flubs.Description: Voronoi cells with height influenced by the distance to the cell's edge, creating ring-like or ridge effects.

Flubs.Name: P
Flubs.Description: The default look for this geo-variant, suitable for creating mountainous terrain with prominent peaks.

Flubs.Name: A
Flubs.Description: A mix between the P and M forms, blending characteristics of both for varied terrain features.

Flubs.Name: S
Flubs.Description: Generates individual mountains with fully separated boundaries, emphasizing isolated peaks.

Flubs.Name: M
Flubs.Description: Favors the strongest cell, ideal for creating a large mountain slope or dominant landform.

Flubs.Name: D
Flubs.Description: Emphasizes ridges over cell centers, producing terrain with pronounced ridge lines.

Flubs.Name: Gain
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the contrast or intensity of the Voronoi pattern, amplifying or reducing the difference between cell heights.

Flubs.Name: Clamp
Flubs.Description: Limits the output values to a specified range, preventing extreme heights or depths in the generated pattern.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different Voronoi arrangements.

Flubs.Name: Warp
Flubs.Description: Specifies the type of warp applied to the Voronoi pattern, controlling the complexity of the distortion.

Flubs.Name: Type
Flubs.Description: Specifies the type of warp applied to the Voronoi pattern, controlling the complexity of the distortion.

Flubs.Name: None
Flubs.Description: No warping is applied; the Voronoi pattern remains unaltered.

Flubs.Name: Simple
Flubs.Description: Applies basic warping to the pattern, introducing gentle distortions.

Flubs.Name: Complex
Flubs.Description: Applies advanced, multi-layered warping for highly intricate and organic distortions.

Flubs.Name: Frequency
Flubs.Description: Controls the frequency of the warp, determining how often the pattern is distorted across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Amplitude
Flubs.Description: Sets the strength of the warp effect, controlling how far the Voronoi cells are displaced.

Flubs.Name: Octaves
Flubs.Description: Specifies the number of detail layers used in the warp, increasing the complexity and richness of the distortion.

Flubs.Name: Transform
Flubs.Description: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the pattern horizontally.

Flubs.Name: Scale X
Flubs.Description: The non-uniform scale of the X axis, stretching or compressing the pattern horizontally.

Flubs.Name: Scale Y
Flubs.Description: The non-uniform scale of the Y axis, stretching or compressing the pattern vertically.

Flubs.Name: X
Flubs.Description: Offsets the Voronoi pattern along the X axis, shifting its position horizontally.

Flubs.Name: Y
Flubs.Description: Offsets the Voronoi pattern along the Y axis, shifting its position vertically.

Name: Warp
Description: Warp can take the terrain and "warp" the shape creating more believable shapes or alter simple shapes into a more complex formation. It can help breakup masks too.

Flubs.Name: Warp
Flubs.Description: The size of the warp noise. Controls the scale of the distortion pattern applied to the input.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: The size of the warp noise. Controls the scale of the distortion pattern applied to the input.

Flubs.Name: Strength
Flubs.Description: The strength of the warp noise. Higher values produce more pronounced distortions.

Flubs.Name: Z Scale
Flubs.Description: Vertical axis scale for the noise, affecting the intensity of the warp along the Z (height) axis.

Flubs.Name: Warp Source
Flubs.Description: Selects the noise or pattern used as the source for the warp. Choose from built-in options or provide a custom source.

Flubs.Name: PerlinFBM
Flubs.Description: Uses Perlin fractal Brownian motion noise as the warp source, producing smooth, natural distortions.

Flubs.Name: VoronoiR
Flubs.Description: Uses Voronoi (R) noise as the warp source, creating cell-like, ridged distortions.

Flubs.Name: VoronoiP
Flubs.Description: Uses Voronoi (P) noise as the warp source, suitable for generating mountainous or peak-like distortions.

Flubs.Name: VoronoiA
Flubs.Description: Uses Voronoi (A) noise as the warp source, blending characteristics of other Voronoi types for varied effects.

Flubs.Name: VoronoiS
Flubs.Description: Uses Voronoi (S) noise as the warp source, emphasizing separated, individual cell boundaries.

Flubs.Name: VoronoiM
Flubs.Description: Uses Voronoi (M) noise as the warp source, favoring dominant cells for strong, directional warping.

Flubs.Name: VoronoiD
Flubs.Description: Uses Voronoi (D) noise as the warp source, emphasizing ridges and linear features in the distortion.

Flubs.Name: Perturbation
Flubs.Description: Applies additional random displacement to the warp, increasing the irregularity and complexity of the effect.

Flubs.Name: Complexity
Flubs.Description: The complexity of the warp noise source. Higher values add more detail and layers to the distortion.

Flubs.Name: Roughness
Flubs.Description: The roughness of the warp noise. Higher values (especially above 0.5) create harsher, more jagged distortions.

Flubs.Name: Normalized
Flubs.Description: Specifies whether the noise is normalized. Normalization ensures the output remains within a standard range.

Flubs.Name: Edge Behaviour
Flubs.Description: Determines how the warp handles the edges of the input, preventing visible seams or artifacts.

Flubs.Name: Edge
Flubs.Description: Applies standard edge handling, which may result in wrapping or stretching at the borders.

Flubs.Name: Mirror
Flubs.Description: Edge pixels are mirrored, creating seamless, reflected borders for the warp effect.

Flubs.Name: Modulation
Flubs.Description: The amount of modulation to use from the Modulation input (if connected), allowing external control over the warp intensity.

Flubs.Name: Modulation Direction
Flubs.Description: Sets the direction of the modulation, controlling how the modulation input influences the warp.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process. Changing the seed produces different warp results.

Flubs.Name: Iterative
Flubs.Description: Number of warp iterations to apply. More iterations increase the complexity and layering of the distortion.

Flubs.Name: Iterations
Flubs.Description: Number of warp iterations to apply. More iterations increase the complexity and layering of the distortion.

Flubs.Name: Mode
Flubs.Description: Specifies the mode used for iterative warping, affecting how each pass is calculated and applied.

Flubs.Name: Bitmap
Flubs.Description: Applies the warp using standard bitmap-based processing for each iteration.

Flubs.Name: VectorField
Flubs.Description: Uses a vector field to guide the warp, allowing for more directional and flow-based distortions.

Flubs.Name: VectorFieldIntegral
Flubs.Description: Integrates the vector field over multiple passes, producing complex, cumulative warp effects.

Name: WaveShine
Description: Generates wave-like reflective or rippling patterns useful for stylized surfaces and water-like forms.

Flubs.Name: Global
Flubs.Description: Specifies the current animation frame or time step for the wave simulation, allowing for frame-by-frame control or preview.

Flubs.Name: Frame
Flubs.Description: Specifies the current animation frame or time step for the wave simulation, allowing for frame-by-frame control or preview.

Flubs.Name: Octaves
Flubs.Description: Sets the number of detail layers (octaves) used in the wave pattern, increasing complexity and realism with higher values.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: Randomization seed for generating unique wave patterns. Changing the seed produces different wave arrangements.

Flubs.Name: Ripples
Flubs.Description: Controls the speed at which ripples animate across the surface, affecting how quickly the pattern evolves over time.

Flubs.Name: Animation Speed
Flubs.Description: Controls the speed at which ripples animate across the surface, affecting how quickly the pattern evolves over time.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: Sets the scale of individual ripples, with larger values producing broader, more widely spaced ripples.

Flubs.Name: Amplitude
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the height or intensity of the ripples, making them more or less pronounced.

Flubs.Name: Direction
Flubs.Description: Specifies the primary direction in which ripples travel, simulating wind or current-driven movement.

Flubs.Name: Speed
Flubs.Description: Controls the movement speed of the ripples, determining how fast they propagate across the surface.

Flubs.Name: Wind Patch
Flubs.Description: Sets the strength of the wind patch effect, increasing the impact of wind on the wave or ripple pattern.

Flubs.Name: Intensity
Flubs.Description: Sets the strength of the wind patch effect, increasing the impact of wind on the wave or ripple pattern.

Flubs.Name: Animation Speed
Flubs.Description: Controls the speed at which ripples animate across the surface, affecting how quickly the pattern evolves over time.

Flubs.Name: Size
Flubs.Description: Sets the scale of individual ripples, with larger values producing broader, more widely spaced ripples.

Flubs.Name: Contrast
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the contrast of the wind patch effect, making the difference between calm and windy areas more or less pronounced.

Flubs.Name: Lighting
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall brightness of the rendered wave surface, affecting how light or dark the result appears.

Flubs.Name: Brightness
Flubs.Description: Controls the overall brightness of the rendered wave surface, affecting how light or dark the result appears.

Flubs.Name: Sun Azimuth
Flubs.Description: Sets the horizontal angle of the sun, determining the direction of sunlight and resulting highlights or reflections.

Flubs.Name: Sun Elevation
Flubs.Description: Sets the vertical angle of the sun above the horizon, affecting the length and intensity of highlights and shadows on the waves.

Name: Weathering
Description: Creates weathered color or mask variation that simulates dirt, fading, and environmental wear.

Flubs.Name: Primary
Flubs.Description: Sets the scale at which weathering effects are applied. Lower values target fine details, while higher values affect larger terrain features.

Flubs.Name: Scale
Flubs.Description: Sets the scale at which weathering effects are applied. Lower values target fine details, while higher values affect larger terrain features.

Flubs.Name: Creep
Flubs.Description: Simulates gradual movement and spreading of weathering effects across the terrain, softening transitions and blending weathered areas.

Flubs.Name: Amount
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the overall intensity of the weathering effect. Higher values produce more pronounced weathering.

Flubs.Name: Washed Out
Flubs.Description: Toggles if colors are faded or desaturated, mimicking the effect of prolonged exposure to the elements.

Flubs.Name: Inverse
Flubs.Description: Inverts the weathering effect, applying it to areas that would normally be less affected, such as recesses instead of protrusions.

Flubs.Name: Dirt
Flubs.Description: Adds darker coloration to crevices, nooks, and sheltered areas of the terrain, simulating the accumulation of soil, organic matter, or moisture.

Flubs.Name: Darker
Flubs.Description: Intensifies the darkness of the dirt effect, making crevices and nooks appear deeper and more shadowed.

Flubs.Name: Post Processing
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the overall hue of the weathered terrain, allowing for color shifts to match desired environmental conditions.

Flubs.Name: Hue
Flubs.Description: Adjusts the overall hue of the weathered terrain, allowing for color shifts to match desired environmental conditions.

Flubs.Name: Saturation
Flubs.Description: Controls the intensity of colors in the weathered terrain, from muted to vibrant.

Flubs.Name: Lightness
Flubs.Description: Sets the overall brightness of the weathered terrain, affecting how light or dark the final result appears.

Name: Whorl
Description: Whorl applies multiple vortex-like distortions across the terrain to create large-scale warping. Very useful for creating massive landscapes without a patterning in the noise and for creating slightly surreal or alien landscapes.

Flubs.Name: Stretch
Flubs.Description: Whorls appear as stretched, interconnected formations.

Flubs.Name: Spin
Flubs.Description: Whorls appear as round, independent formations.

Flubs.Name: Whorls
Flubs.Description: The number of whorls to add to the terrain.

Flubs.Name: Power
Flubs.Description: The strength of the distortion applied with each whorl.

Flubs.Name: Seed
Flubs.Description: The randomization pattern or seed for the node's process.
